title: Setting your hourly rate and minimum charge for short-stay turnover
audience: Owners of short-stay turnover businesses who need a base hourly rate and a per-turnover check before they quote hosts.
learningOutcomes: Separate billable hours from non-billable hours, and calculate the time available to bill.
Calculate a base hourly rate from the owner's own costs and income target, then compare it with local evidence.
Set a minimum charge for short jobs, and explain it to a client before the visit.

instruction.heading: What moves the rate for turnovers
instruction.body: The rate depends on the cleaner's speed and reliability, the size and condition of the property, how tight the booking gap is, and the cost of running the business. Beyond Pricing says turnover frequency and stay length drive the fee (vendor source, 28 October 2026). Use your own costs first, then compare with the vendor labour benchmarks by city: Melbourne $60 an hour, Sydney $55, Brisbane $50, Perth $50, Adelaide $50 and Darwin $40 (vendor data, not verified).

instruction.heading: Counting the hours that can be billed
instruction.body: Paid hours include travel between properties, quoting, admin, marketing, training, equipment care, sick days and leave. Jobber's general guide puts billable time at about 60 to 80 per cent of working hours, which is not an Australian figure. Check your own log against it. If you can bill 60 of every 100 paid hours, the costs of all 100 must come from the 60, so the rate is about 1.67 times the rate for a fully billable week (CALC).

instruction.heading: Building the rate from costs and income
instruction.body: Add the annual running costs (insurance, vehicle, equipment, linen and products, phone, software, marketing and accounting) to the income you need, including leave and super where you pay wages. Business.gov.au says on-costs such as super, leave and tax belong in the hourly figure (1 October 2026). Divide the total by billable hours. Business Victoria advises including total overheads and reviewing prices about every three months (no date shown).

instruction.heading: Test the rate against the per-turnover band
instruction.body: Convert the rate into a per-turnover figure by multiplying it by the time a turnover takes. Then compare the result with the vendor band for the property size, such as $90 to $130 for a general two-bedroom turnover (Beyond Pricing, 28 October 2026). If the result falls below the band, check your hours and costs before you accept the work at that price.

instruction.heading: Set a minimum for short visits and extras
instruction.body: A short visit, such as a quick reset between two guests, still costs travel and set-up. Contractor+ suggests setting a minimum from the full visit cost, divided by one minus the target margin, with the minimum covering travel, set-up and cleanup (23 September 2026). Its figures are illustrative. Gap: the research did not find a minimum per turnover for short-stay cleaning. State any minimum in writing before the visit.

procedure: Estimate paid working hours in a year, then subtract travel, admin, marketing, training and leave to find billable hours.
List the annual running costs, including insurance, vehicle, equipment, linen, products, phone, software and marketing.
Add the income needed, with leave and tax allowances confirmed by a registered tax agent.
Divide the total by billable hours to find the base rate.
Convert the rate into a per-turnover figure, and check it against the vendor band for the property size.
Set and state any minimum for short visits, and review the rate each quarter.

workedExamples.situation: [ILLUSTRATIVE] A solo cleaner plans for about 1,800 paid hours a year and expects to bill 60 per cent of them. Annual costs and the income needed total $60,000 (illustrative). A two-bedroom turnover takes about 1.5 hours (illustrative).
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What base rate is needed, what does a two-bedroom turnover earn at that rate, and how does it compare with the vendor band?
workedExamples.reasoning: Billable hours are 1,800 x 0.60, which is 1,080 (CALC). The base rate is $60,000 divided by 1,080, which is $55.56 an hour. At 1.5 hours, one turnover earns $83.33 (CALC). The Beyond Pricing general band for a two-bedroom turnover is $90 to $130 (vendor, 28 October 2026). At this rate the turnover falls below the band's lower figure, so the cleaner checks whether the 1.5 hours is realistic, whether the costs are right, and whether the band fits this trade. The Melbourne vendor labour benchmark of $60 an hour is close to the illustrative rate, but it is a vendor figure and is not used to set the rate.

commonErrors.error: Setting the rate from a vendor labour benchmark without costing the work.
commonErrors.prevention: Build the rate from your costs and billable hours, then compare with the benchmark.

commonErrors.error: Pricing as though every paid hour could be billed.
commonErrors.prevention: Subtract travel, admin, marketing, training and leave before you divide.

commonErrors.error: Taking turnovers below the band without checking the hours.
commonErrors.prevention: Check the time per turnover and the costs before you accept a price below the band.

commonErrors.error: Using a city benchmark for a different city.
commonErrors.prevention: Use the benchmark for the city it names, and label any other city's figure as unverified.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Price display: show the total price including GST (business.gov.au, 18 January 2024). The research did not confirm the rules for minimum or call-out charges, so check current ACCC guidance before publishing one.

Where you employ cleaners, the Cleaning Services Award may set their pay: Level 1 adult minimum of $25.85 an hour with a 25 per cent casual loading from 1 July 2025 (Fair Work Commission). The 2026-27 rates were not checked.
Tax treatment of leave and super for a sole trader was not confirmed. Check it with a registered tax agent before the rate is published.
This lesson does not grant a cleaning licence or insurance. Licence rules for turnover cleaning were not researched, so check the rules for the state where you work.

qualityStandard: Billable hours are calculated from a logged or estimated month, not assumed.
The base rate is built from the owner's costs and income target, and is compared with local evidence.
A minimum charge is set and stated before any short job.
documentationEvidence: Annual costs and income worksheet, with the source and date of each cost
Billable hours calculation showing the non-billable deductions
Price sheet showing the base rate, the minimum charge and the review date
summary: Price a turnover from billable hours, not paid hours, and check the result against the band.
Vendor labour benchmarks are references. Build the rate from your own costs.
Gaps: no government turnover rate, minimum per turnover or levy rate was found in the research.

knowledgeChecks.question: A turnover cleaner can bill 60 of every 100 paid hours. How should the rate be built?
options: From all paid hours, so the rate looks lower
From billable hours, so costs and income come from the work that can be billed
From the rate a holiday-home owner says is normal
From the highest vendor figure on any site

knowledgeChecks.question: Why should a short reset between guests have a stated minimum?
options: Travel and set-up do not shrink with a small job
Hosts expect every turnover to cost the same
A minimum replaces the booking calendar
Short turnovers need no set-up time at all

knowledgeChecks.question: What is the right use of a vendor labour benchmark?
options: A price to quote straight from
A reference to compare with your own rate, labelled as unverified
A legal minimum for every turnover
A substitute for your own costs and billable hours

sourceReferences: business.gov.au, 'Choose a pricing strategy', https://business.gov.au/products-and-services/choose-a-pricing-strategy, page metadata dated 1 October 2026. Supports: on-costs such as super, leave and tax belong in the hourly figure.

Jobber Academy, 'What are billable hours', https://getjobber.com/academy/what-are-billable-hours/, published 5 November 2024, last modified 20 July 2026. Supports: billable time is about 60 to 80 per cent of working hours; a general range, not an Australian figure.

Business Victoria, 'Develop a pricing strategy', https://business.vic.gov.au/business-information/finance/pricing-for-profit/develop-a-pricing-strategy, no date shown. Victoria. Supports: include total overheads and sales costs in the price; review prices about every three months.

Beyond Pricing, 'Short-term rental cleaning fees (Australia)', https://beyondpricing.com/au/blog/how-much-should-you-charge-for-cleaning-fees-in-your-australian-holiday-rental, dated 28 October 2026. Vendor source; short-stay fee data. Supports: per-turnover bands by property size; move-in and move-out bands by bedroom count; a $120 per-turnover illustration; city labour benchmarks; fixed rates suit smaller properties and hourly rates suit larger or luxury homes.

Contractor+, 'Minimum Service Call Charge: A Contractor's Pricing Guide', https://contractorplus.app/blog/minimum-service-call-charge, 23 September 2026. Supports: a minimum can be set from the full visit cost divided by one minus the target margin, and should cover travel, set-up and cleanup. The page labels its figures illustrative; none are used here.
business.gov.au, 'Display prices', https://business.gov.au/legal/fair-trading/display-prices, page metadata 18 January 2024. Supports: displayed prices should show the total price, including GST.

Fair Work Commission, Cleaning Services Award (MA000022), https://awards.fairwork.gov.au/MA000022.html, variation effective 1 July 2025. Supports: Level 1 adult minimum hourly rate of $25.85 and a 25 per cent casual loading. The 1 July 2026 position was not checked.

State Revenue Office Victoria, 'Register now for the short-stay levy', https://sro.vic.gov.au/news/register-now-short-stay-levy, published 4 March 2025. Victoria. Supports: the levy applies to stays under 28 consecutive days from 1 January 2025; booking platforms and owners or tenants who accept bookings directly must register. The page does not state the rate.
Notes: 1,800 paid hours, the $60,000 target and the 1.5-hour turnover are illustrative. The Melbourne, Sydney and other city labour figures are vendor data and unverified.
